mockmob-original-stimulus-diverse-d5b819.text: Rain had washed the chalk game from the lane. The children arrived with fresh chalk and began drawing again. One child remembered the old squares as longer; another insisted that the turning square had been on the left. They argued until a passing neighbour asked whether the new game had to reproduce the old one. After a moment, they drew a wider turning square in the middle. Their feet soon covered the fresh lines with pale dust. From her doorway, the neighbour could no longer tell which marks belonged to yesterday and which belonged to the game they had just invented.

mockmob-original-stimulus-diverse-474bae.text: In a fictional class, the teacher first asked pupils to propose titles for a shared story. She collected their proposals and read the full list aloud. Only then did the class vote on the listed titles. After the votes had been counted, she wrote the selected title on the story's cover. This account establishes what happened without claiming that a vote is always the best way to choose a title.

mockmob-original-stimulus-diverse-c0e210.text: In this fictional account, Jaya noticed that a plant's label had become unreadable. She checked the plant's identity in the garden's own planting record. Having found the recorded name, she wrote it on a new label. She then replaced the unreadable label with the new one. The sequence establishes the order of her actions without making an outside claim about the plant itself.
